test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-II Official Paper-I (Held On: 20 Jan, 2025)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I, you and she/ have been working happily/ in the same company and in the same branch/ for the last nine years.

options.text: in the same company and in the same branch

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. I, you and she .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In English, the correct order for pronouns in a compound subject should be: Second person (you), third person (he/she/they), and then first person (I).
 
• Thus the correct phrase should be "you, she and I" to follow the standard pronoun order.
 
• The error in "I, you and she" is the placement of pronouns in the wrong order.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When listing multiple people, the polite order usually followed in English is "you, he/she/they, and I".
 
• This helps in setting a respectful tone, placing the focus on others before oneself.
 
• Examples:
 
 
• Correct: "You, she, and I are attending the meeting."
 
• Incorrect: "I, you, and she are attending the meeting."
